abstract: The Rat Genome Database (RGD, https://rgd.mcw.edu) is a multispecies knowledgebase and the primary online resource for genomic, genetic, phenotypic, and disease data for rat. In the past 6 years, RGD has incorporated new data, including three new species, two rat reference genome assemblies, eight rat strain de novo assemblies from Dr Peter Doris' group, and variant data for 118 unique strains from the Hybrid Rat Discovery Panel. Systematic manual curation of metadata and consistent reprocessing of RNA-Seq data from the GEO database have resulted in the addition of a substantial dataset of standardized transcriptomic data. RGD's disease-centric focus has continued with the creation of four new disease portals, bringing the total number of portals up to sixteen and three existing portals have been updated. Four of RGD's data mining and analysis tools were redesigned with a cleaner, more intuitive look and feel and additional functionality. RGD's primary genome browser has been upgraded to JBrowse 2, a browser designed to facilitate analyses across species and between assemblies within a species. To support researchers wanting to learn more about using RGD's tools and data, RGD has begun a project to improve and expand the website's help pages and video tutorials.
